(1) the flow is highly aerated, with air bubbles and droplets extending down to the bottom; (2) turbulence is enhanced in comparison with single-phase flows; and (3) the turbulence is enhanced in proportion to the number of air bubbles and droplet clusters.

1) air-water flows over steeply inclined steps exhibit very high turbulence levels; 2) the turbulence is generated by the entrainment of air bubbles and liquid droplets, and is proportional to the amount of particles; 3) the flow structure is characterised by the presence of large clusters of bubbles and droplets; 4) the clusters are formed by the interaction between air-water flow and the steps, and are characterised by the same size and shape as the air-water flow
the flow down a stepped chute is characterised by very intense turbulence, and that this turbulence level is directly proportional to the number and the size of the entrained air bubbles.

the flow structure of air-water flows down steep channels is characterised by high turbulence, high air-water mixing, high levels of aeration and a significant number (up to 50%) of clusters in the flow.
a significant fraction of the flow energy is used in entraining and mixing air and water.
air-water flows down a staircase chute exhibit very strong aeration and turbulence, and that these two processes interact strongly with each other.
